problem: Most VLM-based VLN-CE methods predict low-level actions (turn 15°, forward 25 cm, stop) at every step. This gives ambiguous supervision, myopic decisions and dozens of VLM calls per episode. The one prior pixel-based attempt, DualVLN, is a hybrid two-stage action-then-pixel design.
motivation: The bottleneck is the interface between VLM reasoning and executable motion, not only VLM capacity. The image plane is the VLM's native input, so a single pixel can ground a navigable goal and be back-projected to a 3D waypoint. This allows longer-range decisions with far fewer VLM queries.
key_idea: Reformulate VLN-CE as pure navigable pixel grounding: the VLM outputs one pixel, either in the RGB region (back-projected to a waypoint) or in auxiliary directive regions (left/right/bottom, meaning turn left, turn right, stop). It is supported by a visibility-aware keyframe memory.
insight: The output interface matters a great deal. With the same setup, pure Pixel gets 54.1 SR vs 32.9 for one-action and 43.7 for the hybrid Action-Pixel (Seq), while using 7.75 calls vs 46.62. Compact history is also key: ViKeyMem matches uniform sampling (54.1 vs 56.1 SR on R2R, better on RxR) at about half the inference and training cost, and removing the trajectory overlay drops SR to 48.7. The execution horizon ablation shows t=5 is best: t=1 gives 36.1 SR, and unlimited execution drops to 40.5 SR because the agent cannot replan.
method: Pixel-grounding interface: the VLM autoregressively outputs a text coordinate 'XXX, YYY' in [0,999]. RGB-region pixels are back-projected with depth into 3D waypoints and tracked by a ShortestPathFollower local planner, which executes at most t=5 low-level actions per VLM call.

Auxiliary directive regions: the current image is padded on the left, right and bottom, and pixels there map to Turn_Left, Turn_Right and Stop, so all decisions share one coordinate space. GT labels: Stop if within 1.0 m of the goal; a turn direction if no future waypoint is visible.

GT pixel construction: project the farthest visible future oracle waypoint onto the image, with visibility verified by a project-reproject check (error < 0.6 m). This gives 2.64M training samples from R2R-CE and RxR-CE English.

ViKeyMem: keyframes are selected when (1) the frame is not visible from the last keyframe, (2) at least one future waypoint is visible, and (3) at least two distinct future waypoints lie within a 45° forward FOV. Blue past-trajectory dots are overlaid on each keyframe. This gives about 4-5 keyframes per 100 steps, with at most 8 used.
Visual semantic embeddings: learnable directive and trajectory embeddings are added to the tokens overlapping the directive regions and trajectory overlays, so the VLM can tell them from regular RGB.
Coordinate-aware losses: the total loss is CE + 0.3·L_num (L1 on normalized soft coordinates from the expected digit values) + 0.03·L_ang (1-cos of the angle from the bottom-center anchor).
Oscillation fallback: after 20 consecutive left-right oscillation actions, the decision is overridden by a forward pixel (500,970).

setting.backbone: InternVL3 (Qwen2.5 LLM), fine-tuned; vision encoder frozen
setting.training_data: 2.64M samples derived from R2R-CE (653,820) and RxR-CE English-US (664,502) and English-IN (1,331,460) oracle trajectories, one epoch; no external data (no EnvDrop/DAgger/VQA)
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (90° FOV, padded to a square and resized to 448) plus keyframe history; depth is used for back-projection
setting.action_space: a predicted pixel back-projected to a 3D waypoint, executed via ShortestPathFollower as low-level FORWARD 25 cm / TURN 15° / STOP; directive-region pixels map to turn/stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (depth is used for back-projection; oracle trajectories are used only for training labels and history selection)

numbers.extra: no external data; 7.75 VLM calls per episode

results: Goal2Pixel-7B reaches 52.7 SPL on R2R-CE (+3.5 over JanusVLN's 49.2) and 44.7 SPL / 63.0 nDTW on RxR-CE. The 2B model reaches 54.1 SR / 52.5 SPL on R2R-CE, above JanusVLN's 52.8 SR. On RxR-CE SR it trails JanusVLN (51.4). Compared with direct action prediction, SR improves by 21.2 points with about 6x fewer VLM calls.
limitations: Requires reliable depth to back-project pixels into 3D waypoints.
Trained and evaluated only on indoor benchmarks, with a small qualitative real-world test (16 trials) and no outdoor validation.
ViKeyMem can miss fine-grained details and short-term motion cues; oscillation between left and right turns needs a heuristic fallback.
